script.1:
1. 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
M: Good afternoon, Grand High School students. This is Mr. Owen, your vice principal. Our school’s dance competition is next Friday. So, I want to ask all dance teams to check their performance schedule for the competition. We have a very tight schedule since there’ll be more than 15 teams and we need to finish the competition by 5 p.m. The performance schedule will be posted tomorrow morning on the auditorium’s door. Once again, don’t forget that all dance teams should check the performance schedule. Thank you for your cooperation.
script.2:
2. 대화를 듣고, 여자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
M: Amy, your workspace looks so different!
W: Does it? I just put some familiar stuff like family photos and postcards from my travels on my desk.
M: They really look nice.
W: You know what? I think having familiar things around makes us feel more comfortable.
M: Really? I usually don’t put any familiar stuff on my desk because I don’t think it would shift my feelings.
W: When I’m stressed, I feel relaxed at the sight of my family photo on the desk.
M: Hmm. That’s interesting.
W: If you try to look at something familiar, you’ll feel more comfortable.
M: I guess you’re probably right.
W: I do think you’ll feel relaxed when you have those familiar things around you.
M: I see. I should try it.
W: You definitely should.
script.3:
3. 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
M: Hey, everyone. It’s Kevin Allen from K.Allen Channel! Do you ever endlessly watch multiple TV episodes in one sitting by yourself? Even though everyone needs time alone, I strongly believe that spending time together with friends makes life more meaningful. Think back to when you tried a new restaurant with friends or had an unplanned adventure with them. Those shared meaningful experiences don’t just create wonderful memories. They also strengthen your bonds with your friends and provide support when you try something new. As you plan the week ahead, make sure to meet friends and create meaningful moments together. Remember, every person needs these connections to feel fulfilled.
script.4:
4. 대화를 듣고, 그림에서 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
W: Honey, look at this photo. It’s from a trip with my dad when I was a child.
M: Can I see it more closely?
W: Sure. Do you see the palm tree on the beach?
M: It’s really beautiful. Wow, there are also two boats!
W: Yeah. They look nice on the water.
M: Oh, there’s a man wearing sunglasses.
W: That’s my dad. He seems to be enjoying the weather.
M: I recognize the girl in the heart-patterned tube.
W: Right, that’s me. I was in the tube most of the day.
M: It looks like you had fun! By the way, is that a ball on the chair?
W: Yes, my dad and I played with the ball from time to time.
M: You know, we should go there with our children.
script.5:
5. 대화를 듣고, 남자가 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
W: Hey, Mr. Davidson! Runners Day is going well, isn’t it?
M: Definitely, Ms. Clark! I set up the race lines this morning, and I also handed out water bottles.
W: Wow, you’ve been busy! I helped with the warm-up stretches.
M: That’s great. Earlier, I noticed some students were unsure about where to go.
W: I saw that as well, so I guided them to their event areas.
M: That was really thoughtful of you.
W: Thanks. Then, are you all done with everything?
M: Not yet. I’ll announce the winners for the running events later this afternoon.
W: Oh, you’re the one who’ll call out the winners’ names after each race?
M: Yep! I’ve practiced the runners’ names. I really don’t want to mess up in front of everyone.
W: I’m sure everything will go smoothly.
M: I hope so, too.
script.6:
6. 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
M: Hello. How may I help you?
W: Hi, I’m looking for cleaning supplies.
M: Well, we have glass cleaner, paper towels, and more over here.
W: I need glass cleaner and paper towels. How much are they?
M: A bottle of glass cleaner is $5. But the price of paper towels depends on the type.
W: I need two bottles of glass cleaner. What types of paper towels do you have?
M: A pack of reusable ones is $30, and a pack of regular ones is $20.
W: Okay. I need one pack of reusable paper towels.
M: Good. You want two bottles of glass cleaner and one pack of reusable paper towels. Right?
W: Yes. Can I use a coupon that I got online?
M: Let me see. [Pause] Yes, you get $3 off the total.
W: Great. Here’s my credit card.
script.7:
7. 대화를 듣고, 남자가 Old Ridge 퍼레이드에 갈 수 없는 이유를 고르시오.
W: Hey! The Old Ridge parade is this afternoon. It’s going to be so cool with music, costumes, and giant balloons! Want to come with me?
M: I’d love to, but I can’t make it today.
W: Really? Are you feeling sick? You looked tired yesterday.
M: No, I’m fine.
W: Then, is it because of your part-time job?
M: Actually, I have the day off.
W: I see. Oh, you haven’t finished your essay for the writing class, have you?
M: It’s nothing like that. I already finished it.
W: Can you tell me what’s going on?
M: I promised my little brother I’d help him with his homework this afternoon.
W: That’s really nice of you. I’ll take a lot of photos and send them to you later.
M: Thanks. Let’s go together next time.
script.8:
8. 대화를 듣고, Booktoon Workshop에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
W: Dad, could you look at this flyer?
M: Oh, it’s about the Booktoon Workshop.
W: Yes. I’ve been really into creating my own stories and illustrating them, but I’d like to learn more.
M: All right. Where’s the workshop taking place?
W: It’s at the Sunvilles Art Gallery. We’ve been there many times.
M: Yes, I know that place. [Pause] Hmm. The workshop provides classes on developing multiple characters and drawing action scenes. You must be very interested.
W: I am. It also has special lectures by invited speakers. One of them is Natalie Moodies, my favorite artist.
M: Oh, I’ve heard you mention her before.
W: Right. You know, there are only 15 spots open for each class, and the registration deadline is June 9th.
M: There’s not much time left. Let’s get you registered right away.
W: Dad, you’re the best!
script.9:
9. 2025 Summer Prehistoric Life Camp에 관한 다음 내용을 듣고, 일치하지 않는 것을
고르시오.
W: Good morning, students and parents. I’d like to tell you about the 2025 Summer Prehistoric Life Camp. This is an exciting opportunity for students from ages 14 to 17 to experience the lives of prehistoric people. The camp will run for two days from July 24th to July 25th at the Green Hill Mountain Campground. Participants will experience fun activities like dressing as prehistoric people and practicing hunting and gathering skills. In addition, they’ll learn how to craft prehistoric tools and pottery. Participants need to bring their personal items but not camping equipment. The registration fee is
$100 and is not refundable. Sign up today for an incredible trip to the past.
script.10:
10. 다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 남자가 구입할 베트남어 학습 앱을 고르시오.
W: Hi, Tim. What are you up to these days?
M: I’m planning to go to Vietnam for a business trip this fall.
W: Awesome! I guess you need to know Vietnamese.
M: That’s right. So, I’ve been looking for a language learning app for Vietnamese.
Can you help me?
W: Of course. Let me see. What’s your budget?
M: I’d like to keep it under $20 a month.
W: That’s reasonable. How’s your Vietnamese?
M: Well, it’s not great. So, the advanced level isn’t right for me.
W: Okay. What do you want to focus on when learning the language?
M: Since this is my first trip there, I need to learn a lot of new vocabulary.
W: Alright, so you have two options left that would work.
M: Which one do you think is better?
W: Because you’re a businessman, I think the app that uses newspapers would be a great choice.
M: I agree. I’ll go with that one. Thanks for helping me choose!

11. 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 대한 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
M: Ms. Baker, it’s a beautiful day. Could our class go outside today to take a group photo with you after class?
W: Good idea, Harry. Why don’t you ask everyone in the class if they all want to take a picture?
M: Actually, I already did, and they all said yes.

[3점] W: Hi, Will. You seem worried. What’s wrong?
M: Hey, Kate. The student council meeting is tomorrow. I’m a little nervous because it’s my first meeting as the school president.
W: Don’t worry too much. You’ll do just fine.
M: You did a great job as the school president last year. So, I’m wondering if you can help me review what to do.
W: Sure! The first thing you’ll do is start the meeting with a greeting.
M: You’re right. And then I’ll introduce myself.
W: Okay. After that, you should outline your vision for the year.
M: Sounds good. Next, I’ll go over the plans for the semester.
W: So far so good. You also need to lead the discussion about the topics for the meeting.
M: That’s everything, isn’t it?
W: Just one more thing. Be sure to thank everyone for their participation.

script.15:
15. 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Steven이 Anna에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
[3점] M: Steven and Anna are teachers in charge of their school library. They’re making a list of books to buy for the upcoming school year. Anna wants to include only classic literature and non-fiction books recommended by experts in the field of education. However, after talking with students, Steven realizes that students love science fiction and fantasy books that are not on the list. He thinks students will be happier and read more if the library has science fiction and fantasy books. So, Steven wants to suggest to Anna that on their list they should include the books students are interested in. In this situation, what would Steven most likely say to Anna?

script.16:
[16～17] 다음을 듣고, 물음에 답하시오.
W: Hello, everyone. Today, we’ll start by discussing how different countries are working to reduce carbon emissions. As you might know, Sweden was the first country to introduce carbon pricing and had the highest carbon tax in the world in 2023. The country is aiming to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 59% by
2030 compared with 2005. Also, Denmark is working to source at least half of its energy needs from renewables by 2030. The country’s energy mix has diversified to include more biofuels, wind and solar generation. Next, Hungary plans to generate 90% of its energy from carbon-free sources by 2030. Part of this plan includes financial support for the purchase of zero-emission vehicles and a huge increase of solar power. Lastly, France is aiming to achieve a net zero carbon economy by 2050. The country is reducing its reliance on fossil fuels and investing in renewables. These countries’ efforts to lower carbon emissions are clearly standing out. After a short break, we’ll explore the world’s biggest carbon polluters.
